lead: Wichita plumbing deals with clay soil, hard water, storms and cold snaps. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Wichita.
risk: cracked sewer lines in clay soil, hard water scale and frozen pipes
risk_short: sewer lines, hard water and frozen pipes
why: College Hill, Riverside and Delano have homes from the 1910s to 1950s with galvanized supply lines and clay or cast-iron sewer laterals. Clay soil shrinks and swells with the weather and cracks them.
Cold snaps freeze pipes near exterior walls and in crawl spaces. Many homes have basements that need sump pumps after heavy rain.
water: Wichita's water comes from Cheney Reservoir and the Equus Beds aquifer. It is hard, so scale builds up in water heaters and on fixtures.
problems: College Hill, Riverside and older areas
tips: Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
Test your sump pump each spring.
areas: PipeMend works in College Hill, Riverside, Delano, Old Town, Crown Heights, Rockhurst and every other Wichita neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits and local plumber licenses come from the Metropolitan Area Building and Construction Department (MABCD). Kansas has no statewide plumber license.

faq.a: Kansas has no statewide plumber license. In Wichita and Sedgwick County, the Metropolitan Area Building and Construction Department licenses plumbers and issues permits.
